steps.content: My father was a hero. He said justice and light are eternal, and he fought for them.
But many, many heroes, died easily on a journey ten years ago. Their deaths were meaningless.

steps.speaker: News
steps.content: In N.F. 103, the FAC's large-scale battle ended in total failure. The number of deaths is not disclosed, with no further explanation. According to leaked information, the destination was the DisSea, with survival odds at zero.

The FAC was widely criticized, its status plummeted to a point where the City Council and Nirvana could manipulate it. My father also became a laughing stock. People called him a hero, but in their hearts, they called him a "wronged soul."
I asked, "father and his mates... all fought for justice and died defending the city-state. Why did it end like this? Doesn't everyone want justice?”
They respond with silence, mockery, or by turning their faces away in disgust. Eventually, someone speaks up, claiming that these "wronged souls" never saw the truth... that justice is a lie...

And they said, In this era, one can be randomly stripped of their rights, and evil can go unpunished. Reality is filled with fog and conspiracy, with interests, hatred, and desire all towering above justice. Blindly believing in it is foolish, and those who die for it... deserve to.

I wanted to argue back, but I choked. Whenever I begin to doubt, bad things always happen. I started to develop a terrible intuition that everything was going downhill, and what's worse... most of the time, it was right.
If justice exists, where is it now? Why doesn't it show itself? The world is falling apart, creating such a massive black hole... why is it being ignored? Why isn't anyone filling it?

steps.speaker: News
steps.content: In N.F. 104, Nirvana withdrew from the West District. A major explosion occurs in mine W-31, causing over ten thousand deaths. The organization claimed it was an accident, and after an investigation conducted by Paradeisos's investigators, this explanation was accepted...
The black hole grows larger, and I can't escape it. I have to do something. I can't just watch as my world collapses with it... I have to do something, I...

steps.speaker: Coquelic
steps.content: The Garden won't believe your righteous talk, it won't believe any of you. Everything that demands submission in the name of love and nobility is a filthy lie. All sacrifices made for these extraneous things are proof of ignorance.

W-31 was not an accident, it was planned. I checked their asset transfers, they're all riddled with irregularities. My intuition tells me this is evil, the same evil that my father and the others faced. If no one will bring them to justice, then I will. I must go!

When someone from Paradeisos went to Nirvana, I lay in wait near Nirvana's headquarters. I got shot at; many people came to hit me, to catch me, labeling me a Sinner. I didn't care—I fought back and managed to stab one of them.
...But it was she who protected me amidst the hail of bullets.
...Is that so? You came here to prove the justice in your heart...
You must be reaching your limit, to resort to such drastic measures...
There's no need for this... It's not time yet, you have a long way to go... Listen to me...
Justice exists, without a doubt. I've seen it with my own eyes.
In another pure, real world... where every facet of the human heart is laid bare... there, I saw justice... and it exists forever...
Right now, someone is standing up for you. Once you grow up, it will be your turn to fight for them...
In this way, what you believe in will surely...
...Christina...

steps.speaker: Shalom
steps.content: Did you have a nightmare?

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: ...Shalom...?

steps.speaker: Shalom
steps.content: Yes, it's me. I'm sorry, I'm late.
She doesn't say anything else, but reaches out to hold Christina's hand. Both of their hands are icy cold.

Christina's vision gradually clears, the nightmares are gone, there's no more bloodshed, no more killing. The little detective, covered in wounds, stares blankly at Shalom, as if she hasn't yet woken from the nightmare, tears rolling uncontrollably down her cheeks.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Sob... I'm sorry... I'm sorry...

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: I stabbed you... I mistook you for a bad guy, I even wanted to kill you...

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: I'm just like them, a jerk who hurts others... I'm sorry...
The girl's emotions pour out, and Shalom just watches. After a while, she finally lifts her hand and pulls the girl into her arms.

steps.speaker: Shalom
steps.content: Don't say that. You didn't hurt anyone, you're the one who got hurt.
Her forehead rests against Christina's, constantly comforting her.

steps.speaker: Shalom
steps.content: Justice is always there, it's already in your hands, you've grown.

steps.speaker: Shalom
steps.content: You've been doing very well.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: Sob... Waaaah...
